blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—The prosecution in the International Criminal Court (ICC) wants information on the sudden surge of drug-related killings by the Philippine National Police (PNP) and the “contradicting” narratives of self-defense by five more witnesses to be admitted as evidence. In a filing released early Thursday, the prosecutors told the Trial Chamber (TC) III to consider the prior recorded testimonies and the associated documentary evidence of individuals referred to as “P-0025” and “P-1382” before former President Rodrigo Duterte begins trial for crimes against humanity. “The two witnesses elaborate on the increase of killings during Mr Duterte’s presidency and the contradiction between [REDACTED] […]...
